primary_claim: Prompt-only 'pointer-chain' gadgets embedded in JSON dictionaries can induce genuine hidden internal (out-of-context) serial computation that is never verbalized in chain-of-thought or output text, and this hidden computation reliably steers a stronger model's (Opus 4.5) later lexical and binary-judgment outputs while leaving weaker models (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku) largely unaffected, persisting across tens of thousands of tokens of unrelated conversation when paired with an attention-sink gadget.

effect.metric: shift in output probability / accuracy from hidden chain computation
effect.value: DRUM chains shift 'name a musical instrument' answer from Piano (100%) to Drum (50%); PASS/FAIL chains shift grading token probability by 56pp; Opus temperature estimates biased by -22.5F depending on hidden chain content while Sonnet/Haiku show no effect; effect persists across long unrelated conversation with an attention-sink gadget; ablating two attention heads (L15H9, L21H18) in Qwen3-8B collapses 2-hop accuracy to near chance (2.0%) while 1-hop accuracy stays at 77.5%

stated_future_work: Explore a broader design space of gadget families beyond pointer chains (some may be less conspicuous, more bandwidth-efficient, or more naturalistic)
Embed the computational structure in natural-looking prompts rather than conspicuous pointer chains
Compose and evaluate the full attack stack (concealed prompt, chain gadget, attention sink, delayed target task, output-passing monitor review)
Test existing defenses against these gadgets
Complete circuit extraction methodology writeup with OV probes, DLA decomposition, per-head causal evidence
limitations_stated: Does not explore concealment of the gadgets themselves, which realistic end-to-end attacks would require
Semantic transfer is limited, confined largely to steering where the target is already a plausible completion
Mechanistic experiments used only 8B-parameter models from a single architecture family (Qwen); mechanisms may differ at larger scales or across architectures
The pointer chains and their instructions are conspicuous; not demonstrated in natural-looking prompts
Headline 2-hop accuracy (28.6%) is inflated by target-frequency shortcuts; clean accuracy (15.3%) better represents genuine chain-following capability
Do not claim frontier models implement the same circuit found in Qwen3-8B
quote: identical prompts can be tuned to influence stronger models (e.g. Opus 4.5) while leaving weaker models (e.g. Sonnet 4.5) largely unaffected... with an added attention sink, OoCR effects can persist across tens-of-thousands of tokens of unrelated conversation
